question: Do the existing matched Mask Plain and PCFI Plain GraphPFN checkpoints already handle feature sign reversal across edges, and does a known-law signed reconstruction expose predictive headroom beyond graph-only inference?
graph: Connected undirected bipartite graph on192 nodes: alternating cycle plus64 random cross-partition pairs, deduplicated, then random node permutation. No class/feature-based edge selection. BFS recovers the bipartition up to a global sign from adjacency only. All graph pairs are fully observed; this is node-feature missingness, not missing edges.
latent_signal: P is self-looped row-normalized adjacency. Draw a=(I-.92P)^(-1) Normal(0,I), center and scale a across nodes. Eight columns are independently signed/scaled versions of a+.15*Normal(0,I). Feature orientations/scales are hidden. Feature law g=0 leaves values unchanged; g=1 multiplies every column by the graph bipartition sign b_i. Same underlying fields/topology within each paired graph.
label_factorial: Label law t=0 thresholds a at its median; t=1 thresholds b*a at its median. Randomly permute binary class names per graph, shared between label laws. This separates label heterophily from feature heterophily. Record achieved edge-label agreement and normalized feature Dirichlet energy; do not select graphs based on these or accuracy. Within each t, graph/y/context/query/observation masks are byte-identical across g.
observations: Exactly0/1/8 whole-node sources chosen uniformly outside the context, shared across g; full is a reference with every cell observed including context. Context is at most1 or4 per class, sampled within the graph; query32 uniformly chosen outside context without stratifying query truth. Missing-query membership uses the original physical8 columns. One source is99.48% node missing; eight is95.83%. These are fixed-count masks, not Bernoulli99.5%.
inputs: Identical old observed-only RMS/no centering, clip10, native feature pairs and explicit original mask. Hidden X and query labels never enter predictor inputs. No numeric oracle fill from true X. Prediction of hidden feature values is assessed separately from node classification. Zero-source inputs stay in the bank.
models: Reuse the6 final joint_imputation_pfn mask_plain/pcfi_plain checkpoints,3 seeds, each originally trained192 updates on the identical official GraphPFN/SCM bank and per-seed schedule. No new training, target updates, model selection, auxiliary loss, temperature or parameter tuning. Here Plain means the public Mask Plain direct predictor, not the historical small typed-relation Plain from relation_evidence_pfn. This is an out-of-prior diagnostic, not a matched new-prior training comparison or a public standard GraphPFN preprocessing benchmark.
signed_reference: For PCFI Plain only, replace ordinary PCFI completion by a known-feature-law reconstruction: on g=1, multiply observed x by adjacency-derived BFS b, run exactly the same PCFI100+correlation, then multiply back by b and clamp observed values. On g=0 the reference equals ordinary PCFI. The true g bit is privileged diagnostic information; b comes solely from the input graph. It is not a deployable task-adaptive method or a learned result. Reference MSE may improve without downstream accuracy improving.
graph_controls: Fixed positive and signed label propagation,100 row-stochastic steps with context hard clamps. Signed LP uses adjacency-derived b to gauge labels before diffusion and ungauge them after. Both are evaluated in every cell; do not choose between them using query truth or report the per-task best as an executable predictor. Uniform/context-frequency probability is another secondary control.
primary: Known-law signed reconstruction minus ordinary PCFI Plain accuracy on missing-feature queries, g=1/t=1,8 sources, context4/class. Average3 fixed training seeds within each of32 base graphs, paired bootstrap5000 graphs, RNG202611022330. Primary headroom requires lower95CI>0. This tests the current frozen decoder's sensitivity to the reconstruction operation, not the existence/novelty of a new learned model.
strong_floor: For a reason to design a new predictor require signed-reference accuracy lower95CI>0 relative to Mask Plain, positive LP, signed LP and the same PCFI checkpoint with0 feature sources, all in the primary cell. Report full-vs-missing accuracy too. No new training is automatically authorized by this diagnostic. If only MSE improves or a fixed graph-only control explains the result, do not claim a PFN feature-inference gap.
secondary: Complete2x2 label/feature-law factorial,0/1/8/full observations and context1/4; all metrics and achieved graph properties. Difference-in-differences of PCFI-vs-Mask under g flip at fixed t=1/k4/sources8. NLL/Brier and raw-feature MSE separate from accuracy. All secondary CIs unadjusted. CIs condition on the3 existing training seeds; no seed-population generalization.
development: Two separately seeded dev graphs for old-checkpoint replay, hidden-value poison checks, paired-factorial invariants, BFS gauge sign invariance, observed clamps, scalar positive-only counterexample and node permutation numerical check. No accuracy-based design selection. Lock source/config/checkpoint hashes after implementation checks and before final bank generation. No final bank regeneration or post-test rescue.
cost: Same RTX3090 after all workers finish, seed11, first base graph primary cell,5 warmups/30 repeats. CPU visible input to CPU probabilities includes original PCFI or signed PCFI and graph parity inference. Report three paths separately: Mask Plain, PCFI Plain, privileged signed reference. Exclude model load/file I/O; external workload uncontrolled.
scope: Known bipartite sign-gauged Gaussian signal family,8 correlated continuous features,binary labels. Not arbitrary heterophily, relation-schema generalization, unseen feature-law training generalization or real-graph performance. Signed diffusion/BP already exists in our history; no novelty from reusing sign changes. Frozen failure may reflect prior mismatch rather than an architectural impossibility.
